Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 103, verse 1–3:

Tafsir of Surat al-'Asr (the Declining Day)

It is Meccan.

They mention that 'Amr ibn al-'As visited Musaylima al-Kadhdhab [may Allah curse him] [[Addition from A.]] after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had been sent and before 'Amr had embraced Islam. Musaylima said to him: "What has been revealed to your companion in this period?" He said: "A short, eloquent surah has been revealed to him." He said: "And what is it?" He said: "By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except for those who believe and do righteous deeds, and advise one another to truth, and advise one another to patience." Musaylima reflected for a moment and then said: "And a similar one has been revealed to me." 'Amr said to him: "And what is it?" He said: "O Wabr, O Wabr, you are only two ears and a chest, and the rest of you is a quick, scurrying creature." Then he said: "How do you see it, O 'Amr?" 'Amr said to him: "By Allah, you know that I know that you are lying." [[There is room for doubt about the soundness of this account, for 'Amr ibn al-'As's embracing of Islam preceded Musaylima's claim to prophethood. Musaylima al-Kadhdhab claimed prophethood in the tenth year of the Hijra, and he had come to the Prophet ﷺ with his people in the tenth year of the Hijra, as in the Sirah of Ibn Hisham (3/74). 'Amr ibn al-'As embraced Islam in the eighth year according to the most correct view, as in al-Isabah of al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar (3/2). Then I came upon what al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar transmitted in al-Isabah (3/225): that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent 'Amr ibn al-'As to Bahrain, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died while he was there, and that he passed by Musaylima and gave him a pledge of safety, then said to him: "Muhammad has been sent with a great matter, and you have been sent with trivial matters..." and he mentioned something like the account, and attributed it to Ibn Shahin in al-Sahabah. Based on this, what is mentioned here would be after 'Amr ibn al-'As's embracing of Islam, not before it, and Allah knows best.]]

I have also seen that Abu Bakr al-Kharaiti cited in his well-known book "Masawi al-Akhlaq," in its second part, something of this or close to it [[I did not find it in the printed edition of Masawi al-Akhlaq. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar mentioned that Ibn Shahin transmitted this account through al-Layth from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal: "That Qurrah ibn Hubayrah came to the Messenger of Allah ... " Then he mentioned that the Messenger of Allah sent 'Amr to Bahrain, and he mentioned something like the account. See: al-Isabah (3/225).]].

Al-Wabr: a small creature resembling a cat, whose largest feature is its two ears, while its chest and the rest of it are ugly. Musaylima wanted to compose from this nonsense something with which to oppose the Qur'an, but that did not succeed with the idol-worshippers of that time.

Al-Tabarani mentioned, through the chain of Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from 'Abdullah ibn Hisn [Abu Madinah], who said: "When two of the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ met, they would not part until one of them recited 'Surat al-'Asr' to the other, to its end, and then one of them would greet the other with salam." [[al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. (5097), "Majma' al-Bahrayn."]]

Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "If people contemplated this surah, it would suffice them."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

Al-'Asr: the time in which the movements of the children of Adam take place, of good and evil.

Malik said, from Zayd ibn Aslam: it is the afternoon, but the well-known view is the first.

So Allah, exalted is He, swore by it that mankind is indeed in loss, that is, in damage and destruction, ﴿except for those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. He excepted from the human race from loss those who believe in their hearts and do righteous deeds with their limbs, ﴿and advise one another to truth﴾, which is performing acts of obedience and abstaining from what is forbidden, ﴿and advise one another to patience﴾ in the face of calamities and decrees, and in bearing the harm of those who hurt them, from among those whom they enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil. End of the Tafsir of Surat "al-'Asr," and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.
